abstract: Local ribosome accumulation near transmembrane domains (TMDs) may report cotranslational events in membrane-protein biogenesis, but its spatial organization and stress responsiveness remain unclear. Saccharomyces cerevisiae ribosome-profiling data were reanalyzed using a replicate-aware, TMD-centered workflow. Two untreated wild-type baseline samples showed maximal accumulation approximately 75 nucleotides downstream of annotated TMD starts. At this position, 2896 TMDs met strict eight-sample coverage criteria; 2892 were testable using quasi-likelihood negative-binomial models of target-window counts relative to gene-wide non-TMD coding background. Forty-one TMDs showed an ER-stress effect in wild-type cells, six in eS7-4KR cells, and 22 showed a genotype-by-stress interaction at false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05. Interaction-effect directions were concordant across models, but only eight of the 22 primary interactions met FDR < 0.05 in both target/background models; 16 remained significant after global correction across 11 positions. Baseline signals were heterogeneous. Aromatic-residue fraction remained associated with local accumulation in a prespecified joint model. Mean-based upper-tail topology associations weakened with one-TMD-per-protein resampling; continuous protein-level comparisons were nonsignificant. Functional enrichment was sensitive to the number of tested TMDs per gene and was treated as exploratory. These results identify spatially resolved, stress- and eS7-associated ribosome-occupancy differences without equating footprint enrichment with proven translational pausing.
